caseno: Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 17084, 2189 and 10026 of 2005.
lawyer:
Md Khurshid Alam Khan, Ruhul Quddus with Md Toufiq Imam, Advocates—For the Petitioners. 
Md Helaluddin Mollah, Deputy Attorney-General — For the Opposite Party.
parties:
Nayan Miah & another ----- Accused-Petitioners 
Vs.
State ----- Opposite Party
full_judgment:
Sheikh Abdul Awal J: All these 3(three) Rules were issued on 3 separate applications at the instance of 4 accused persons for bail in Sessions Case No. 238 of 2004 arising out of CR Case No. 81(2) 2004 corresponding to Netrokona Police Station Case No. 24(2) 2004 under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code, now pending in the Court of Additional Sessions Judge, Netrokona and thus the Rules are taken up for hearing simultaneously and are being disposed of by this common judgment. 

 2. The short facts of the case are that one Mrs Kulsum Akhtar as informant on 21-2-2004 lodged the first information report with Netrokona Police Station alleging, inter alia, that on 21-2-2004 at about 9-00 AM the accused (1) Ruptan son of Late Abdus Salam alias Engil Meah (2) Polash son of Arab Miah (3) Moklas son of Harmuj Ali (4) Sadek son of Lilu Miah (5) Nayan Miah (6) Kashem both sons of Abdul Ali (7) Jamal son of Chuta Abu (8) Bazlu Son of Farhad Khan (9) Jahan son of unknown, son-in-law of Suraj Ali (10) Saiful son of Nabal Ali all of Police Station Netrakona, District Netrokona with 4/5 unknown person after being armed with deadly weapons like nem dao, kirich, churi, kural and lathi attacked her elder son Sujan Miah aged about 25 years in the Muktijuddha Bazar premises. At one stage the accused-persons forcibly took her son if a road distance near about 100 yards of west side of the Muktijuddha Bazar, while all accused persons tied him with rope and then accused Ruptan cut vein of victim's leg, accused Polash dealt a kirsch blow on his right leg, accused Moklas dealt a kirich blow on the victims left knee, accused named Sadek, Nayan. Miah, Kashem one after one stabbed with kirich on the knee of victim's right leg, accused Jamal with knife cut the finger of victim's right leg, accused Jahan dealt a kirich blow on the upper portion of the left ankle of the victim and accused Bazlu and Saiful beat him indiscriminately with lathi as a result of which the victim Sujan Miah sustained serious bodily injury. On hearing hue and cry witness Nos. (1) Touhid Miah son of Moti Meah (2) Sohel Rana son of late Jahed Khan (3) Gunu Miah son of late Hossain (4) Rashed son of late Ahmed rushed to the place of occurrence and then the accused persons left the place of occurrence. At that point of time the victim discloses the entire incident to them. It has been further alleged that on hearing the incident police arrived at the place of occurrence and they shifted the informant's son to Netrakona Hospital but on the way the victim Sujan Miah succumbed to his injury. Upon the aforesaid allegation Netrakona Thana Case No. 24(2) 2004 under sections 302/ 34 of the Penal Code was started. 

 4. Ultimately, the case was transmitted in the Court of Additional Sessions Judge, Netrokona for trial. 

 5. Mr Md Ruhul Kuddus with Mr Md Taufiqul Inam, the learned Advocates appearing for the accused petitioners in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 2189 of 2005 and Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 10026 of 2005 submits that the accused petitioners are innocent they have been falsely implicated in the case at the instance of the informant party. Mr Ruhul Kuddus in the course of argument has taken us through the first information report and then submits that the admitted premises of allegation shows the accused petitioner Jahan dealt a kirich blow on the upper portion of the left ankle and accused petitioner Bazlu dealt lathi blow on the person of the deceased victim Sujon Miah indiscriminately, although it appears from the FIR that some of the accused persons cut the vein of leg of the victim and inflicted fatal knife and kirich blows on the person of the victim Sujon Miah, which might have caused his death. He submits first information report dose not disclose that the accused-petitioners committed any offence liable to be found guilty under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code. Finally, Mr Md Ruhul Kuddus, the learned Advocate submits that on consideration of the materials on record this Court at the time of issuance of the Rules granted ad-interim bail to the accused petitioners namely Jahan and Bazlu in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 2189 of 2005 and Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 10026 of 2005 respectively and both of them after being enlarged on ad-interim bail did not misuse the privilege of bail and, as such, their ad-interim bail should be conformed for the ends of justice. 

 6. Mr Khurshid Alam Khan, the learned Advocate appearing for the accused petitioner Nos. 1) Nayan and 2) Kashem Miah in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 17084 of 06 submits that the accused petitioners are absolutely innocent; they have been falsely implicated in the case. He submits that the allegation as attributed in the body of the first information report against the accused petitioners is in lump and not so severe, inasmuch as the First Information Report itself discloses that accused Nayan and Kashem dealt Kirich blows at the knee of the victim's right leg. MR Khan further submits that both these accused petitioners have been languishing in custody since long and some of the accused persons namely 1) Jamal 2) Shahidul 3) Real 4) Milon Munshi 5) Jahan 6) Bazlu standing on the same footing have already been granted bail and, as such, the accused petitioners should be enlarged on bail. 

 7. Mr Md Helaluddin Mollah, the learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing for the State, on the other hand, opposes the Rule. He submits that there is specific overt act against this accused petitioners in the body of the first information report, police after investigation submitted charge sheet and others under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code and the case is now pending for trial and, as such, at this state the accused petitioners may not be enlarged on bail. Although, the learned Deputy Attorney-General could not show any scrap of paper that the accused petitioners, namely Bazlul and Jahan, after being enlarged on ad-interim bail in any manner misused the privilege of bail. 

 8. We have heard the learned Advocates of both the sides, perused the Rule petitions and supplementary affidavit along with connected papers as annexed therewith. It appears from the first information report that the accused petitioner Jahan dealt a kirich blow on the upper portion of the left ankle of the victim, accused petitioner Bazlu dealt a lathi blow on the person of the deceased victim Sujon Miah indiscriminately, accused petitioner Nayari and accused petitioner Kashem dealt kirich blows at the knee of the victim's right leg. So, it seems to us the part allegedly played by the accused petitioners in commission of the crime and nature of injury manifested in post-mortem report is not so much grave to endanger the life of a person. It also appears that the confessional statement of co-accused named Moklas is exculpatory in nature, Further, it appears that the first information report was lodged on 21-2-2004 and police submitted charge sheet on 31-5-2004 and thereafter, the case was transmitted for trial in the last part of 2004 and since then to till now the prosecution in all examined only 5 witnesses, out of 21 charge sheeted witnesses, which glows that the trial will take a long time. Consequently, we hold that the trial is unduly delayed due to the negligence of the prosecution. Moreover, some of the accused standing on the same footing have already been enlarged on bail Hence, we find substance and force in the sub-mission of the learned Advocates for the petitioners. 

 9. Considering all the aspects of the case, practically its progress, we are inclined to enlarge the accused petitioners on bail. 

 10. In the result the Rules are made absolute. The ad-interim bail granted by this Court to the accused petitioners Bazlu and Jahan in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 2185 of 2005 and Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 10026 of 2005 respectively, is confirmed. The accused petitioner Nos. 1) Nayan Meah and 2) Kashem both sons of Abdul Ali @ A Ali, Village Gabragati, Police Station Netrakona and District Netrakona may find bail to the satisfaction of the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Netrokona in which the case is pending for trial.
